item.title: Here are the Apple deals actually worth picking up ahead of Black Friday
item.author: Sheena Vasani
item.content:encoded: A new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch can make a great holiday gift, but they can also take a pretty big dent out of your budget. That’s especially true this year, as rising hardware prices have made MacBooks and other Apple devices even more expensive. Fortunately, Black Friday offers a chance to save, especially since great deals are already available on a wide range of Apple devices. Some discounts even extend to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro, which have dropped to new lows. Most of the discounts below are promoted as Black Friday deals, but we’ve also included a few that aren’t part of the shopping event but have “coincidentally” dropped in price in the last week or so. Black Friday isn’t until November 27th, however, so some prices could fall further in the coming days. Apple is also kicking off its own Black Friday shopping event that day, offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases. That said, if you don’t want to wait, we think the deals below are already worth taking advantage of.Earbud and headphone dealsYou can buy the on sale at Walmart for around $89 ($40 off), which is $20 shy of their best price. Apple’s last-gen earbuds lack active noise cancellation, but they still deliver good, relatively bass-rich sound, even if they don’t quite match the newer AirPods 5. They also offer voice call quality on par with the latest AirPods Pro. Read our review.The are down to $419 ($130 off) at Amazon, which is $19 shy of their best price to date (Best Buy and Target also have them for about $10 more). Like the original, Apple’s latest over-ear headphones feature a luxurious build consisting of aluminum, steel, and a mesh fabric, but they offer better sound and noise cancellation. The new H2 chip also enables features like adaptive audio and live translation. Read our review.If you want over-ears and are comfortable going without active noise cancellation, the are down to $79.99 ($120 off) at Target in pink and white through November 22nd, marking a new low price. Amazon also has the pink headphones on sale for $79.99, while other colors are $20 more at both retailers. The headphones are a noticeable improvement over their predecessor, delivering more detailed sound and support for lossless audio. They also last up to 50 hours on a single charge, while their memory foam ear cushions make them comfortable enough for long listening sessions. Read our review.The are down to around $89.95 ($80 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and Target, nearly matching their lowest price to date. The wireless earbuds feature a slick, eye-catching transparent option and solid noise cancellation, especially at this price. They’re also exceptionally comfortable, with four ear tip sizes to help you find a secure fit. Sure, you don’t get wireless charging, but they offer IPX4 water resistance and up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge. Read our review.The recently released 16.3-inch MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR display, 24GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage is on sale starting at $3,249 ($150 off) — a new low price — at Amazon and Best Buy. The redesigned laptop is Apple’s first with an OLED touchscreen, which allows for rich colors and deep blacks. It’s also noticeably thinner and lighter than the non-touchscreen 16-inch MacBook Pro, and features a new Dynamic Island that replaces the notch and provides quick access to controls and notifications. Read our review.The 14-inch M6-powered MacBook Pro is on sale starting at $1,849 ($150 off) at Amazon and Best Buy, which is a new low price. The Pro builds on its predecessor with a faster chip and support for Wi-Fi 7. In our testing, it handled multitasking, photo editing, and occasional video editing with ease while still delivering exceptional battery life. It lacks the newer MacBook Pro’s gorgeous OLED display, but its Mini LED screen still looks great, especially given its smooth 120Hz refresh rate. It also offers excellent speakers and a good selection of ports, including three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, and an SD card slot. Read our review.The is on sale in the 40mm / GPS configuration starting at $199 ($50 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, matching its best price to date. Apple’s newest entry-level smartwatch remains our top recommendation for anyone who wants a basic fitness tracker, as it offers all the essentials alongside an always-on display and Apple’s S10 chip, which enables on-device Siri requests.AirTags, chargers, and other dealsYou can buy the with 128GB of storage and Wi-Fi on Amazon in select colors for $484 ($115 off), which is the best price we’ve seen since Apple’s recent price hikes. It has a smaller screen and a slower chip than the newer model, and it lacks an OLED screen, the Acoustic Display, and water resistance. Still, it’s a great option for reading and everyday use that’s currently more affordable than its $699 successor, with support for Apple Intelligence and the Apple Pencil Pro. Read our review.Apple’s latest Magic Mouse is matching its all-time low of $59.99 ($20 off) at Amazon. The wireless mouse features a touch-sensitive surface that lets you scroll through documents and swipe between apps with simple gestures; it also pairs automatically with compatible Macs and offers support for USB-C.

item.title: 'I just have to reiterate the power that we have as riders' - Lombardia protest ringleader Ben Healy emboldened as he calls for change on rider safety
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: The five minute delay before the start of Il Lombardia at the close of the European season demonstrated the power riders have in forcing better safety in races, according to Ben Healy (EF Education-EasyPost).Rider safety has been the hottest topic in road cycling since the terrible death of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal in the summer. And when that incident was followed by a series of further near-misses during the Italian autumn Classics, something had to give.Healy was the driving force behind what he calls a 'stand' rather than a protest, the peloton delaying the start of Il Lombardia, the season’s final Monument, by five minutes. But, as powerful as the delay was, and as hard hitting and articulate as Remco Evenepoel’s (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) words were, the demonstration was an example of the power riders have."I think we just really wanted to show as riders the power that we had, and that we're not happy," he told in a café close to the bustle of the Rouleur Live show, where he was fulfilling sponsor commitments. "We didn't want to just go at the Lombardia organisers, for instance. You know that's why we chose to do a five-minute stand before the race actually started, and just delay the race, and just show that if this continues, that this is what we can do if we choose to.""I think after that happened [with Tarling] everyone expected something to change, you know, and when we went to Italy, there were what, three cars on the course in separate races over three or four days? And that was pretty clear then that nothing had changed," Healy said. "There has to be a process to make things safer. And I mean, for sure, the UCI is aware of it, but I don't know how aware they are, they’re not on the ground every single race. This is clearly something that is recurring, and it just shouldn't happen ever, having a car on the course, let's just hope the UCI will listen and work with us to make change."If Lombardia was the example of what unity within the peloton can do in bringing an issue to notice, Healy prefers not to commit to what might happen if and when such a dangerous situation occurs again, or worse, should another rider die."I just really hope it doesn't come to that, you know? I just have to reiterate the power that we have as riders and ultimately what we can do if we choose to. "Mistakes can be made, and as long as we're working towards making racing safer, I think that's the most important thing. We don't want to point blame or, like, kick and scream, it’s about being productive and working together to improve the sport for everyone." item.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Clark Griffith
item.author: Kevin Winterhalt
item.content:encoded: Though Clark Griffith is the first man to manage the New York baseball team we now call the Yankees, his time in New York is merely one chapter in a story of one of the giants of baseball’s early history. That’s no shot at Griffith’s time in New York and his importance to the franchise. It’s just he had such an amazing life and career.He was already an accomplished hurler when he came to New York and became the player-manager of the club, in its first season in The Big Apple. And long after he hung up his cleats, he remained an integral part of baseball in the first half of the 20th century. November 20, 1869 (Clear Creek, MO) October 27, 1955 (Washington, DC) 1903-07 (player/manager), 1908 (manager)Clark Griffith was already a grizzled veteran when American League President Ban Johnson named him manager of the New York Highlanders (often called the Americans in the press) prior to the 1903 season. It was the inaugural campaign for the club, which relocated from Baltimore after the Orioles folded following two seasons.The diminutive Griffith (listed at 5-foot-6) was a right-handed pitcher, and a good one, at that. Between 1894 and 1901, he won at least 20 games in a season seven times. His first season in New York was also his last one as a starting pitcher, and he tossed more than 200 innings while managing the club to a disappointing fourth-place finish.Griffith’s pitching days were not over, however. He transitioned to the bullpen and continued to pitch at a high level while trying to steer the Highlanders to a pennant. In 1904 and 1906, he came close, with the club finishing in second place each season, mere games from wining the American League.Modern Yankee fans are used to skipper Aaron Boone getting himself tossed from games, though he was shockingly well-behaved in 2026. He’s far from the first Yankee manager to get the hook, of course. Griffith, by virtue of being the first manager, gets that honor. Like his modern successor, Griffith also got himself suspended for his conduct toward umpires.On Monday, August 27th, 1906, Griffith took umbrage with a safe call at first base while playing St. Louis. As a result, the umpires ordered Griffith off the field. The Highlanders’ skipper took his sweet time about it. Unfortunately for him, AL President Johnson was in the crowd, and the next day he suspended Griffith indefinitely. Yeesh. “Savages in the Box,” this was not. Seems a little harsh. But wait — there’s more. The indefinite suspension might have something to do with Griffith fighting umpire Tim Hurst earlier in the season, which also got him suspended. For that round of fisticuffs, Griffith received a five-day suspension. His ban in August lasted a week.The Highlanders bottomed out on Griffith’s watch in 1908, and in June he decided it was time for him to move on. Owner Frank J. Farrell tried to dissuade the disheartened Griffith, but to no avail.“It was fighting against fate,” Griffith told , “And I knew when I had enough. I do not know who my successor will be, but I understand [Kid] Elberfeld is mentioned for the place. If that is so, I wish him the best of luck, and I hope my successor will pull the team out of the rut and place them where they belong.”Griffith’s warm feelings for the club definitely did not last forever. At his death, the noted, “Mr. Griffith had two pet dislikes in his lifetime. One was John McGraw and the other was the New York Yankees.”Griffith’s time in baseball was by no means done when he left New York. Most famously, he eventually found himself in Washington, where he leveraged his assets to obtain a 10 percent stake in the notoriously bad Senators. “First in war; first in peace, and last in the American League,” the old saying went.Griffith won five pennants in nine years before again relying on his assets to buy a majority share in the franchise. By 1920, he’d transitioned out of the dugout and into the owner’s box, ending a 20-year managerial career where he won 1,491 games (26th most all-time). In 1924, his Senators finally won the World Series, upsetting the New York Giants. They would win further pennants in 1925 and 1933 as well.Clark Griffith is almost certainly the most important person in the history of Washington baseball, with all due respect to Walter Johnson. He’s also the answer to an obscure yet important bit of trivia. Who was responsible for the tradition of US presidents throwing out the first pitch? It was Griffith, who in 1910 asked President William Howard Taft to toss out the first ball. Taft obliged and the rest is history.Griffith was also key to baseball’s relationship with the U.S. government and military during both world wars. In World War I, he organized an initiative to get baseball equipment for every American soldier overseas. He even got President Woodrow Wilson to chip in. During World War II, he was one of the people who helped convince President Franklin Roosevelt to keep baseball playing.He’s the only man in baseball history to have played, managed, and owned a team for at least 20 years each. Clark Griffith was elected to the Major League Baseball Hall of Fame in 1946. His Senators would eventually pass to his son, Calvin, who would move them to Minnesota in 1961 to become the Twins (and become rather infamous in his own right).Clark Griffith died on October 27, 1955, in Washington, D.C. In its obituary for the legend, noted what former president Harry S. Truman had said about Griffith in 1946 when he had thrown out a presidential first pitch, the tradition Griffith started decades earlier.“Mr. Griffith is a shining example of what this great country of ours can produce.”Happy birthday to the Yankees’ first skipper.See more of the “Yankees Birthday of the Day” series here.

item.title: Shirin van Anrooij to make cyclo-cross debut with Canyon-SRAM alongside Zoe Backstedt next week
item.author: laura.weislo@futurenet.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: Shirin van Anrooij will make her debut with Canyon-SRAM in the upcoming UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup in Ostrava, Czechia, next week, racing alongside Zoe Bäckstedt at the start of a 13-race schedule, the team announced on Friday.She has been training in Malaga, Spain alongside her new teammate and former under-23 cyclo-cross rival Bäckstedt in preparation for the intensive campaign of 11 World Cups, the National Championships and culminating with the World Championships in Oostende, Belgium in January."I'm just really excited and looking forward to starting the season because we've been watching CX racing on TV for a couple of weeks now, and I'm really curious to see how it is amongst the girls again," Van Anrooij said in the team press release."I think Zoe and I are having a good preparation camp here in Malaga, so I can't wait to be on the start line myself, and to see where my level is at.""I'm hoping that I'll reach my best level in cyclo-cross again, and then I'll just have to discover what results this will bring me," Van Anrooij said."I think the biggest goals are, for sure, the Christmas period with a lot of races that I really like – Koksijde, Zonhoven, Gavere, and then the World Championships in Oostende. Worlds is always a big goal for everyone, but I especially look forward to that, with it being a race on the sand in Belgium."After her first year racing in the elite fields last season, with nine races from the end of December through Worlds, Bäckstedt is looking forward to a longer campaign. "I'm really excited for this cyclo-cross season. It feels like it's been two years since I properly raced CX as last year was an extremely short season for me."It's super fun having Shirin as my teammate. Already for training, it's been really beneficial for me to follow her and learn from her. I'm now excited to do our first race together."Although both riders have goals for the early part of the 2027 road season, Canyon-SRAM's performance director Dan Fleeman supports their off-road ambitions."I think cyclo-cross offers several important benefits. From a physical perspective, it develops the ability to repeatedly produce high-intensity efforts, accelerate out of corners, change pace and deal with constantly changing demands. It also requires a high level of anaerobic capacity and the ability to recover quickly between efforts."Technically, the benefits are equally important. CX develops bike handling, balance, coordination and the ability to make decisions under pressure. Riders are constantly adapting to different terrain and conditions, managing their effort and finding the quickest way through a course."Also, I think that there is a mental benefit. CX is an incredibly demanding discipline where you have to be prepared to push yourself outside your comfort zone, deal with mistakes, and keep fighting throughout a race."Their calendar has been designed to focus only on the major races, skipping the Superprestige, X2O Trofee, and HG Cross."The main consideration is quality over quantity. The World Cup offers the highest level of competition, the best opportunities to measure ourselves against the world's leading riders, and the experience of racing on some of the biggest stages in cyclo-cross."We also have to consider the overall demands of the season. Both riders have important road objectives, so we don't want to overload the programme with racing simply for the sake of racing. We would rather be selective, target the important events, and make sure that they arrive at them in good physical condition."Canyon-SRAM 2026-2027 cyclo-cross scheduleFri, Nov 27: UCI World Cup Ostrava (CZE)Sun, Nov 29: UCI World Cup Tabor (CZE)Sun, Dec 13: UCI World Cup Glasgow (GBR)Sat, Dec 19: UCI World Cup Antwerpen (BEL)Sun, Dec 20: UCI World Cup Koksijde (BEL)Sat, Dec 26: UCI World Cup Gavere (BEL)Tue, Dec 29: UCI World Cup Besançon (FRA)Sun, Jan 3: UCI World Cup Zonhoven (BEL)Sat - Sun, Jan 9-10: National Championships (GBR/ NED)Sun, Jan 17: UCI World Cup Benidorm (ESP)Sat, Jan 23: UCI World Cup Hamme (BEL)Sun, Jan 24: UCI World Cup Hoogerheide (NED)Fri - Sun, Jan 29-31: UCI World Championships Oostende (BEL)The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Forbes releases 2026 F1 team valuations
item.author: Samarth Kanal
item.content:encoded: The report puts Ferrari highest at $9.5bn to Mercedes's $9.2bn, putting those two most valuable F1 teams on par with the top half of the NFL's teams, the three most valuable NBA teams, and Real Madrid.F1's 11 teams are therefore valued at an average of $5.2bn and, not including Cadillac - which was absent from the 2025 rankings - the average is up to $5.4bn, a gain of 53% from last year. Haas has made the largest increase in value - of 87%, from $1.5bn to $2.8bn - while McLaren's value has increased 73% to $7.6bn. Scroll down to view the full valuations table.Forbes uses estimated revenue as part of its calculations: from 2024 to 2025, estimated revenue rose 15% to $530m per team. Its report says that McLaren and Mercedes expect to surpass $1bn for the first time ever in 2026 - and only the NFL's Dallas Cowboys and football teams Real Madrid and Barcelona have reached that mark.The report highlights “multiples” as a catalyst for F1 teams' growth: in 2019, F1 teams were valued at 2.3 times their previous season's revenue and the 10 teams (excluding Cadillac) are now valued at 10.3 times last year's revenue on average.This signals a transformation of F1 teams' business models over the last seven years, implying that the value of an F1 team is tied to their huge potential for growth rather than physical assets and historic cashflow. Owning a stake of an F1 team is therefore likened to owning that of a valuable US sports franchise, with F1 teams' revenue multiples now closing in on the NFL and NBA - and well ahead of the NHL, MLB, and European football.The upswing in multiples is, according to Forbes, a consequence of the 2021 cost cap (at $215m for 2026) that limited spending. The cost cap, plus Concorde Agreements, have led Ferrari, Red Bull, Racing Bulls, Mercedes, Haas, and Alpine to be profitable in 2025 - with McLaren expected to hit a profit of $200m in 2026. Mercedes is estimated to have the highest profit of $225m.With just 11 teams on the grid, it's rare to be able to own a piece of an F1 team. Sportico reported in November that Mark Walter's stake in Cadillac is being offered for at least $3bn.Liberty Media CEO Derek Chang recently said that F1 has made “huge inroads” into the United States, a continued area of its focus, while China and India “represent opportunities” both for F1 and MotoGP.In 2027, the values of Mercedes and Ferrari are projected to hit $10bn.F1 teams are 'overwhelmed by interest'Being on the ground here in Las Vegas, it's no surprise to me that Forbes is reporting a 47% increase in the average value of a Formula 1 team.I've been talking to Liberty Media CEO Derek Chang for an upcoming interview in The Race Business this week and listening to him you get a sense of how buoyant the people running the championship feel about its prospects in America. Walk through the city and you can understand why.I've been to all three US grands prix this year. There was a real commercial buzz in Miami and Austin, but here in Vegas it feels like it's reaching fever pitch. As most things do in Vegas. The team commercial directors I've spoken to are almost overwhelmed by the interest. They're scrabbling around for paddock passes or trying to squeeze one more prospect into the Paddock Club. Everywhere you go there's a brand event. American companies are practically throwing money at Formula 1.Look at what F1 itself announced in three days. Standard Chartered upgraded its partnership. Nike signed up. So did Whoop. Who would have imagined, even a few years ago, that there'd be a wearables category on F1's sponsorship list? The series is in rude health.At our Monaco event in June, Aston Martin's Jefferson Slack asked “We're valued at six or seven times revenue. Why is an NBA team valued at 12 times revenue?” Forbes now puts the 10 established F1 teams at an average of 10.3 times revenue. On that measure, much of the gap Jeff saw has already closed.How much weight should we put on the individual numbers? Forbes and Sportico published eight days apart and disagreed by $1.3bn on Ferrari alone. Over the off season we'll revisit our work on team ownership and valuations and look at how the assumptions behind both reports stack up against the deals people have actually done.Perhaps the scrabble for passes is a decent KPI for the scrabble for ownership. There are only 11 teams and yet you can usually find one more pass. If either of the rumoured Alpine or Cadillac stake sales gets over the line before Christmas, we might get a firm data point of what it now costs to get in permanently.Forbes' 2026 F1 team valuations

item.title: Everything that happened in Portimao MotoGP practice
item.author: Eden Hannigan
item.content:encoded: Alex Marquez provided an upset to the expected order as he concluded Friday MotoGP practice at the Portuguese Grand Prix as the fastest rider on his return from surgery. VR46 Ducati’s Fabio Di Giannantonio was narrowly behind Marquez in second, as the satellite Ducati riders proved the manufacturer still had the pace to challenge Aprilia. It provided a slight change to the expected order as Marco Bezzecchi had comfortably led throughout the session, though the rider who was fastest in FP1 was ultimately shuffled to third.KTM’s Pedro Acosta and LCR Honda’s Johann Zarco also showed solid pace consistently in Friday’s running and completed the top five.It was a less straightforward session for the other riders still in title contention, with Marc Marquez and Jorge Martin both flirting with a place in Q1 in the first half of the session. Marquez was ultimately comfortable by the chequered flag as he finished the day in sixth, while it was more touch-and-go for Martin, who narrowly squeezed into the last automatic Q2 spot in 10th. Brad Binder and Fermin Aldeguer were two of the riders who slotted between Marquez and Martin, who was fortunate not to have been pushed into Q1 by the Trackhouse Aprilia pair, as Raul Fernandez took ninth while Ai Ogura was 11th.Iker Lecuona crashed twice on the factory Ducati while replacing Pecco Bagnaia.Pol Espargaro, who came in between sessions for the still-injured Maverick Vinales at Tech3 KTM, also suffered a crash at Turn 1 with 12 minutes left on the clock.1 Alex Marquez (Gresini Ducati) 1m37.350s2 Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) +0.082s3 Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia) +0.172s4 Pedro Acosta (KTM) +0.255s5 Johann Zarco (LCR Honda) +0.258s6 Marc Marquez (Ducati) +0.278s7 Brad Binder (KTM) +0.297s8 Fermin Aldeguer (Gresini Ducati) +0.320s9 Raul Fernandez (Trackhouse Aprilia) +0.351s10 Jorge Martin (Aprilia) +0.408s11 Ai Ogura (Trackhouse Aprilia) +0.509s12 Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM) +0.653s13 Diogo Moreira (LCR Honda) +0.756s14 Jack Miller (Pramac Yamaha) +0.790s15 Fabio Quartararo (Yamaha) +0.912s16 Jake Dixon (Honda) +1.041s17 Luca Marini (Honda) +1.325s18 Alex Rins (Yamaha) +1.342s19 Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) +1.602s20 Pol Espargaro (KTM) +1.746s21 Augusto Fernandez (Pramac Yamaha) +1.942s22 Iker Lecuona (Ducati) +2.016s

item.title: Valve says it might have to raise the price of supply-limited Steam Machines
item.author: Kyle Orland
item.content:encoded: When the Steam Machine first started shipping in June, Valve said it was producing fewer units at a higher price than initially planned because it couldn't secure supplies of scarce RAM and storage components at a reasonable cost. Now, as the last of the initial batch of Steam Machine reservations are finally being fulfilled, Valve says those supply and cost issues will continue into the foreseeable future and may even require a price change."We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels," Valve wrote in a blog post on Thursday. "As a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained."

item.title: Knicks Bulletin: ‘I was raised by Wolves’
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: I thought yesterday’s game was over by the end of the third quarter……only for these fools to nearly drop it. Good thing, they did not.Here’s a bunch of quotes coming off Minnesota as the boys return home once and for all.On finishing the road trip with a victory over Minnesota:“Great to finish off a road trip, getting a win in a pretty tough environment by a well-coached team. It’ll make the plane ride a little bit better going home.”On the Knicks’ fourth-quarter offensive collapse against the Timberwolves:“Our execution the first three quarters was at a pretty high level against this team. And then you give them credit. Fourth quarter, they did a phenomenal job defensively, kind of bogged us down. The ball and the pace offensively in the frontcourt wasn’t popping like it was the first three quarters.”On the Knicks winning the battle for loose balls despite struggling offensively in the fourth quarter:“The thing that saved us was winning the 50-50 ballgame. We were 13-for-14 in that area, and that was huge for us because we had trouble scoring in the fourth.”On beating his former team as an NBA champion with the Knicks:“I was raised by Wolves, but it was Knicks in 5 at the end.”On why the Knicks don’t need to win games convincingly:“For ‘Dancing with the Stars.’ For us, at the end of the day, as long as we win, this team is just trying to stack the number on the left side.”On the importance of winning games in different ways:“If you wanna win a championship, you gotta be ready to win in any way possible, because you never know what the game will be.”On his uncertain contract situation and remaining focused on his responsibilities to the Knicks:“I got a job to do, at the end of the day. I gotta come here and put that jersey on and do what’s best for my brothers and the guys they have in my locker room. So, I’m just here to do my job.”On refusing to let his contract situation distract him from performing:“I gotta put that jersey on and put the best performance out there for my teammates. So, that’s all I really think about.”On his emotional attachment to Minnesota:“I still have so much love for this place. It doesn’t go away. I think it’s actually grown as I’ve been away. I think that, even for me and my dad, we were just driving around the city and just going to places. We went to eat at a spot we love to go here. It always hits home. This is the last place that I got to play basketball with my mom. I got to see the kids be young before now. Jolani, my niece, who was in my rookie of the year photo actually in here, she was a baby, and now she’s in high school. It’s a different part of life, but it’s a part of life that I really enjoy.”On returning to Minnesota as an NBA champion:“It’s always great to be home and to be back here. Nine years of my life, some amazing years, amazing moments. Yeah, it’s special to be back. Obviously, it’s bittersweet to come back with a championship because I wanted to win it here so bad for the city, for Minneapolis, for Minnesota, for all the people who haven’t seen an NBA championship here. But it’s great to be able to come back and to be able to see friends, people I call family here.”On the release of the new Grand Theft Auto game and his excitement to play it:“I haven’t played the game yet, but I’ve heard it’s a hell of a game. So shout-out to Rockstar [Games] and 2K and Take-Two [Interactive]; they did a good job with that one. It’s fun, man. The world is taken over by ‘GTA,’ as it rightfully should be.”On his Grand Theft Alvarado nickname and his history with the video game:“I was a big fan of it before my name. It was just a cool name that I had, so it makes it even better when I play the new one. Got the name for it; now, play the game.”On how much his life has changed since GTA V dropped:“Thirteen years ago, I wouldn’t even be talking to you, I promise you that. It’s a long journey, fun journey, one hell of a ride. Still with it.”On the Knicks nearly blowing their lead against Minnesota:“It was hectic. We gotta get better at finishing a game like that. But it’s a win, 3-1 on the road trip. We’ll take it.”On the criticism Karl-Anthony Towns faced during his Timberwolves years:“Particularly when he started his playoff journey, how much flak he had gotten.”On Towns leading the Wolves to the Western Conference Finals:“We don’t do it without him in all facets of the game, whether it be his defense in the Phoenix series, the only guy who held us in the game in Game 7 in Denver when we had nothing else going until we could find it in the second half. Those are the little moments that spring to mind. There are many others along the way. And he kind of grew into that and then was able to build on that with an experienced team where he fit into in New York.”On watching Towns succeed in the Knicks’ championship run:“It was fun to see him at the heart of it, too. Especially as they were kind of tweaking their offense going along and all of his skills came to the surface through that.”On the similarities between Towns and LaMelo Ball:“They play with a lot of expression to their game and people interpret that or they don’t like that. But it doesn’t mean that A) they’re not super talented players, of course, and B) they can’t play winning basketball. Sometimes it’s as much of the environment that people might be judging them unfairly through, if that makes sense.“They both are really selfless in the way that they play. But maybe some of their expressions and the way that they carry themselves on the court draws a lot of attention and they get judged unfairly for that, too. They’re actually incredibly selfless. They both play with a lot of joy.“They’re incredible people. Just great teammates, fun to be around, always bring the same energy every day. Very coachable.”

Yankees 2026 Roster Report Cards: George Lombard Jr.
item.author: Jonathan Farrar
item.content:encoded: Few positions, or the players manning them, have been debated as intensely as shortstop for the New York Yankees over the last several seasons. Heading into 2026, many fans hoped the club would find a way to move on from the Anthony Volpe experience. However, the club made no external moves and started the season with José Caballero slotted in at the position as the team waited for a rehabbing Volpe to return.Along the way, injuries and performance, both struggles by the incumbents and red-hot play in the minors, led the Yankees to hand the reins at shortstop over to 21-year-old George Lombard Jr. The rookie would spend August, September, and October at shortstop for the Yankees in what really is the throne of NYC. In terms of how it went, the staff here at PSA averaged out to a B-minus. In academic speak, that would mean Lombard understood the core material and performed above average, but did not master the assignment. 42 G, 166 PA, 23 R, 36 H, 4 2B, 1 3B, 7 HR, 22 RBI, 2 SB, .237/.285/.414, 92 OPS+, 93 wRC+, 0.4 fWAR, 1.1 bWAR. Pre-arbitration eligible.Before reaching the show, Lombard was on an absolute tear in the minors. Starting the season in Double-A, he hit .312 with a .971 OPS in 20 games, which earned him a ticket to Scranton. Lombard’s season looked like it might be coming off the rails after an adjustment period, and then he sprained two fingers, which sidelined him for a month and caused him to miss the MLB Futures Game. However, he came back in mid-July and forced the Yankees’ hand right before the Trade Deadline, going on a 14-game heater to the tune of a .377 average, .477 OBP, and 1.081 OPS.On August 4th, after surviving the Trade Deadline himself, and with the Yankees not acquiring an outside option at shortstop, the club called Lombard up to the show. The kid finished the minor league season slashing .284/.411/.498 with 12 home runs. This performance led Baseball America to name him the Yankees’ Minor League Player of the Year for 2026.Lombard’s 2026 season at the professional level, and the basis for our grading, really is a story of three parts. The first was a euphoric honeymoon stage. Lombard committed just one error in his first 14 games and racked up eight Defensive Runs Saved (DRS) in his first 100 innings, looking like a potential Platinum Glove winner. This all came as he homered in his first pro at-bat and slashed .320/.393/.560 with a .953 OPS across his first 25 at-bats. It was too good to be true.After the rise came the fall, as Lombard slumped with the glove and bat. In late August, Lombard made the wrong kind of history, committing an error in six straight games and tying a 105-year-old franchise record. With the stick, big league pitchers started getting him to chase and roll over breaking balls, causing his average to sink to .217 by mid-September. The vibes from some fans really went from “next” to “next Volpe.”To the kid’s credit, he righted the ship down the stretch and saved himself in the third act. From September 9th through the end of the regular season, Lombard’s defense stabilized to league average, and he hit five home runs in his final 16 games. He carried that confidence into the postseason, going 3-for-4 in the Wild Card opener against Boston and finishing October batting .333 (6-for-18), albeit with an error in the ALDS.I’ll save the hype train for future preview articles. However, despite only having an 86 mph average exit velocity, Lombard finished the season pacing for 27 home runs over 162 games. There’s also a lot of room for growth, as Lombard had a 17.3 percent walk rate at Triple-A and only a six percent rate in the majors through his first 42 games, or essentially a quarter of a season. The defense, especially when playing beside a big league-quality third baseman, was fine for someone who was just a few months into being able to buy an adult beverage.Lombard’s minor league season was an A+, while his rookie season comes in at a B-. With some growing pains behind us and a few more likely ahead, here’s to hoping Lombard can continue to improve and develop into a difference-maker. What grade would you circle in red for Lombard’s 2026 season, and what do you predict he’s produce next season?See more of the Yankees Roster Report Card series here.

item.title: US will soon announce root cause behind FAA nationwide ground stop
item.author: Jeremy Hsu
item.content:encoded: The US government will announce soon the root cause of the router outage that led to the third-ever nationwide ground stop issued by the US Federal Aviation Administration. But questions remain about whether the FAA's effort to modernize the national airspace system is being done with all the proper risk assessments and adequate agency oversight of the private contractors involved.The nationwide ground stop blocked flight departures and impacted more than 1 million passengers across the United States for more than four hours on Friday, November 13. More than 12,000 flights were canceled on that day alone, with the number rising to more than 20,000 over the weekend as stranded travelers scrambled to find accommodations or alternative transportation. Some international flights were allowed to depart prior to the broader resumption of air traffic.Nearly one week later, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told news reporters that government investigators are “very close” to figuring out the root cause of the nationwide ground stop, according to CNN. Bedford also said that Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to announce the findings at a news conference as soon as Friday, November 20.

item.title: Vinales withdraws after single MotoGP session in Portugal
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: Maverick Vinales has pulled out of the second-to-last round of the 2026 MotoGP season, replaced by KTM test rider Pol Espargaro.Vinales, who does not have a ride for 2027 and remains limited by the shoulder injury he sustained last year, is now also in doubt for the season finale in Valencia, which was set to mark his final appearance as a full-time MotoGP rider for the time being.The 31-year-old has spent the entire campaign struggling to be competitive due to the after-effects of that 2025 shoulder injury at the Sachsenring. A follow-up operation and various courses of treatment have allowed him to recover his fitness for daily life, but when it came to riding in MotoGP he has encountered persistent issues with pain and inflammation.The lack of any recent competitive track record meant KTM abandoned the plan to promote him to the factory outfit from satellite team Tech3, and he was then left out of Tech3's 2027 line-up, too.Ahead of Portimao, Vinales said that the weekend off between Qatar and Portugal allowed him to improve his condition - but was wary of how his body would react to riding the KTM RC16 again."If I'm riding right now, I mentioned many times, one [reason] is for my salary, and the second is because my team is here, and I want to race for them, and I don't want someone [else] riding my bike."But on Friday, after placing 19th in the opening practice session, with 17 laps completed, Vinales has called time on his Portimao outing."It was a really difficult decision, because I want to keep pushing, but we have decided it is best to stop," he lamented. "The important thing is to avoid any more damage to my shoulder and any dangerous situations on track, and I will continue to focus on my recovery. "It's disappointing, especially after all the work I've put in to get back here, but I have to listen to my body."Tech3 says Vinales "will continue to assess his condition" ahead of the Valencia finale.

item.title: Yankees sign Jonathan Loáisiga to two-year deal
item.author: John Griffin
item.content:encoded: So far this winter, the bullpen has been a clear priority for the Yankees, who saw no fewer than four important relievers from the 2026 season become free agents. After re-signing Tim Hill and bringing back David Bednar on the qualifying offer, the team has now made its third addition to the bullpen, coming to terms with old friend Jonathan Loáisiga on a two-year deal with a team option for 2029.Canal 4 News in Loáisiga’s native Nicaragua had the news late last night, the man himself hinted at it with a picture of the NYC skyline on his Instagram story, and Jorge Castillo of ESPN confirmed it this morning. MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand reported the total outlay of the contract as $18 million across the two years and buyout.Yankees fans are, of course, very familiar with the man nicknamed Johnny Lasagna. Signed as a minor-league free agent in 2016 after a couple years in the Giants’ organization, Loáisiga spent parts of eight seasons with the big league club, and served as the bullpen’s ace fireman/setup man in 2021 and the second half of 2022. Injuries and ineffectiveness plagued the right-hander for the next three seasons, however, and after a lackluster 2025, the Bombers declined his team option for 2026.It turned out to be the best thing for him. After sitting on the market for most of the winter, Loáisiga signed a minor-league free agent deal with the Diamondbacks last January. He made the team out of spring training, stayed healthy for a full season for the first time in five years, and put together one of the best seasons of his career, posting a 2.42 ERA in 67 innings. Perhaps more importantly, his advanced metrics were some of the best of his career, and helps explain why there were so many suitors for the recently-turned 32-year-old (the Mets, Phillies, Dodgers, and Blue Jays were all reportedly in on him).Despite the small time apart, though, Loáisiga is not exactly the same pitcher who Yankee fans remember. Gone are the days where he threw the sinker like Mariano Rivera threw the cutter, i.e., pretty much every pitch. Although it’s still his main offering (he threw it 35 percent of the time last year), that is a far cry from the 54-to-69-percent usage rates from his first Yankees stint; in its stead, he’s upped his changeup, fastball, and cutter.While nobody would ever consider Loáisiga a strikeout pitcher, these changes oversaw a slight bump in strikeout percentage to 18.4 percent from his 16.6-percent rate between 2022-24 and a slight drop in walk rate to a career-best 5.0 percent, all without sacrificing ground-ball rate. The question will just be how his body holds up after an actual full, healthy season.Even with Loáisiga, Hill, and Bednar back in the fold, the Yankees are probably not yet done looking at bullpen arms — assuming they ever truly feel like they have enough bullpen arms. At this point, though, the Yankees have successfully turned it from a “need” to a “want,” as they’re no longer so thin out there that Yerry De los Santos and Angel Chivilli were listed as two of the team’s higher-leverage relief arms on the FanGraphs Depth Chart.One could, of course, absolutely still argue that they still need a big swing-and-miss arm in the ’pen, as they’re still lacking in that regard and not everyone should be a pitch-to-contact guy. As we wait for the league to come to a screeching halt in 10 days due to the owners’ insistence on a lockout, getting some things crossed off the winter to-do list is certainly not a bad thing, and Loáisiga checks another box.

item.title: SpaceX lenders don’t want Elon Musk launching their collateral into space
item.author: Michelle Chan, Financial Times
item.content:encoded: Lenders backing SpaceX’s latest $43 billion debt package, which is secured by its advanced AI chips, have tried to bar Elon Musk from firing the collateral into space as part of his plan for orbital data centers.The world’s richest man has outlined ambitious plans to power AI models with data centers cooled by the vacuum of space. That will require packing satellites full of advanced chips.SpaceX has said it plans to use the chips involved in the debt deal on Earth. But lenders have expressed concerns that if the group later decided to shoot the valuable chips that underpin their loans into space, it would prevent them from reclaiming and selling the semiconductors in the event of a default, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: From plumbing to Picnic PostNL – The Dutch team's newest recruit with dreams of Amstel Gold Race and riding with Wout van Aert
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: The lowest-ranked team in the WorldTour last year, Picnic PostNL, have made plenty of changes to their roster next season, with nine new faces and counting.Joining the Dutch team in their quest for more success in 2027 is Belgian racer Daan Depuydt, who comes on board from Continental squad Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureau Lions.The 23-year-old, who previously raced at amateur level, enjoyed several standout rides this year, including a Tour de Limousin stage win and three top-10 finishes at the Tour de Wallonie. His rise to the WorldTour has been a rapid one, given he was working as a plumber just a few years ago.Depuydt, who also did odd jobs as a gardener and electrician, told that, "Actually, I was never really consciously focused on landing a professional contract. I just raced because I enjoyed it."He primarily raced on the mountain bike as a junior, picking up four Belgian titles before struggling with back injuries. On the road, he raced in Belgium with amateur squad VP Consulting before catching the eye of Baloise-Het Poetsbureau – Sven Nys' team – with a stage win at the Triptyque Ardennais in 2025.He hit the ground running this year, with June's Tour de Wallonie only the second UCI-ranked race of his career after the Antwerp Port Epic in May."I was riding there with broken ribs, because I had a bad fall 2 days before the opening stage," he told . In August, there was another top ride in Limousin, where he finished second on the opening day before winning stage 3."After my second place in the opening stage, I wanted to win one of the remaining 3 stages at all costs. And in the third stage, I struck gold," he said."After the opening stage, I suddenly started receiving messages from teams. But I never thought I'd actually secure a spot – especially after reading an article about how many riders were still without a team for the season."Soudal-QuickStep were among the teams to show interest, though they were already full for 2027. Choosing Picnic PostNL was a no-brainer, he said, despite recent reports of a 'culture of fear' at the team."When the moment finally came to put pen to paper with Picnic PostNL, I didn’t have to think twice. I had a good feeling right from the start of our conversations. They prioritise the riders' interests and are always open to feedback," he said."Sure, it’s a strict team, but name me one WorldTour team that isn't. As a team, you have expectations of your riders, and vice versa. That dynamic can – and should – be a bit strict, provided it’s handled fairly."Depuydt sees himself as a puncheur who excels on shorter climbs while also sprinting well from a small group. He's hoping to race on his home training roads at Amstel Gold Race next season, and is dreaming of racing alongside his idol, Wout van Aert – a goal which shows just how far he's come since his plumbing days."I see myself as a puncheur. Short climbs suit me thanks to my past as a mountain biker. But I have also noticed this year that I am fast. I am not a pure sprinter; I am too light for that. But after a tough race, I can finish well in a reduced group," he said."I've never ridden a race with Wout. I would think it's really cool if that happens next year. If we stand at the start of a race together, I will look for Wout and ride behind him for a bit to take a look at him."If I could just follow him for a little while on a climb, that would be a huge dream come true."The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: WorldTour team ignored by new Collective Cycling Group reform project
item.author: Patrick Fletcher
item.content:encoded: The nascent Collective Cycling Group (CCG), a coalition of teams bidding to overhaul cycling’s economic model, did not seek the involvement of all the WorldTour teams, with Human Powered Health telling they were ignored by the project. The CCG, which is the new version of the failed One Cycling movement, launched publicly on Wednesday, with 24 teams coming together in a bid to "unlock the value potential of professional cycling".Not all 32 teams from across the men’s and women’s WorldTour agreed to sign up to the new company, with Tadej Pogačar’s UAE Team Emirates the most notable of the teams who have declined to be involved. However, one WorldTour team, Human Powered Health, were not even approached. A spokesperson for the US outfit, which has operated in the Women’s WorldTour since 2022, told that senior management were not made aware of the CCG nor of any opportunity to take part in such a project.The complete overlooking of an established WorldTour team raises early question marks over the unity of the CCG, which was described by its CEO Oliver Ciesla as a “broad and inclusive initiative”. Furthermore, it was not billed as a closed shop, with the announcement stating that discussions with other teams are ongoing. The project is largely made up of WorldTour teams but two second-division men’s outfits, Pinarello-Q36.5 and Tudor Pro Cycling are shareholders in the company, too. Contacted on Friday in relation to Human Powered Health's position, a spokesperson for the Collective Cycling Group said: "CCG has brought together a significant group of leading professional cycling teams, and we are open for that group to grow over time."The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Rocket Report: A weekend of ups and downs; Stoke celebrates engine milestone
item.author: Stephen Clark
item.content:encoded: Welcome to Edition 9.20 of the Rocket Report! Last weekend was a picture of the US launch business in miniature, and emblematic of the opposing trajectories of two of the nation's most experienced rocket makers. First, on Saturday, SpaceX completed a perfect midair catch of its Starship upper stage at its launch pad in Texas after spending nearly a day in orbit. The Super Heavy booster was lost at sea, but SpaceX proved it can recover that piece of the rocket on previous flights. While SpaceX showed it is well on the way to fielding a fully reusable rocket, United Launch Alliance suffered its first-ever total launch failure with the Vulcan rocket. That is terrible news for not only ULA, but also the US Space Force and Amazon, which have booked some 70 launches on Vulcan over the next few years. Your faithful correspondents will take a break from the Rocket Report next week for the Thanksgiving holiday, so we'll see you again the first week of December.As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.Europe's leading satellite startup eyes Italian rocket maker. Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe’s first true vertically integrated end-to-end space company, Ars reports. Avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit. ICEYE is, by far, the most successful space startup in Europe, with a valuation of more than $12 billion after the company's most recent fundraising round in June.

item.title: Black Friday Wahoo deals 2026: Kickr Core 2 hits best-ever price, Elemnt computers on sale too
item.author: josh.croxton@futurenet.com (Josh Croxton)
item.content:encoded: With summer behind us, thermal bib tights back in rotation, and a winter of hiding from the rain on Zwift on the horizon, that can only mean one thing: Black Friday is fast approaching. Like mine, I expect your inbox is full of Black Friday promotions, and the latest to land in mine is a huge Black Friday Wahoo rundown; a list of everything we can expect from Wahoo Fitness, the cycling tech mainstay from Atlanta.Wahoo's own Black Friday sale kicks off today - November 20th - with deals across smart trainers, indoor bikes and treadmills, but there are plenty of other deals if you know where to look. So no matter if you're shopping for a new smart trainer, a bike computer, a heart rate monitor, or even a treadmill, you're in the right place to find the best price and the best advice. If you want to take it a step further, you can add on the Zwift Ride v2 smart frame too. This still uses the Kickr Core v2, but the frame replaces your bike, saving you the need to wheel it through your house. It's also more widely adjustable, so you can share it with others in the house. View DealWahoo is slowly branching out into running, and the Kickr Run is its first foray into treadmills. I've not used it, but the general consensus is that it's very good. View DealWhether running or cycling, if you're doing it indoors you'll want a really good fan to help keep you cool. This is still the gold standard in that space, and although the price is steep, mine is still running strong after seven years of regular use. View DealThis is a bit of an odd one as Amazon says its retail price is 624.99. That's not true, it's actually $499.99. However, it's still a nice discount on the biggest model in Wahoo's GPS computer range. View DealIn our opinion, it's likely the best for most people. Great navigation, great features, and very user friendly. View DealThis one's the smallest model in the range. It's perhaps more of a racer's choice, but it also packs more or less all the features of the Roam into a smaller package.That means it's cheaper still, but the smaller screen can be limiting in some cases. View DealThis is the same as the product above, but with the Zwift Cog and Click add-on, which replaces the cassette with a single-speed cog that's compatible with all modern groupsets. The 'Click' then lets you shift virtually in-game, which is silent, unlike the loud clunk you sometimes get from a derailleur. View DealBut before you commit to the V6, consider this, which is potentially better and currently the same price. The Kickr Move uses the same internals as the current Kickr smart trainer, but adds a moveable track to allow you to roll forward and backward under high load, and a few degrees of left-right tilt too.In use, the left-right tilt makes for a slightly unusual ride feel, since it doesn't self-centre like a bike. I often felt I was fighting it with core strength or simply sitting at an angle. View DealThe Zwift Ride V2, paired with Kickr Core 2, is the whole-bike indoor solution, saving your own bike from the wear and tear. Its broad adjustability also means you can share it with others in your home, or try out new positions without changing the fit on your main bike.View DealIf you want to go even more premium than the Zwift Ride and Kickr Core pairing, this Kickr Bike Pro is it. It's broadly adjustable, tilts back and forth to mimic gradients, it's belt-driven so had a completely silent operation, and shifting is silent too. View DealOr a halfway house between the two, the Kickr Bike Shift, which offers the quiet operation and broad adjustability, but foregoes the tilting and a few other features to keep the price down. View DealWahoo is primarily a cycling-focussed company, but it's slowly branching out into running, and this Kickr Run is its first foray into treadmills. View DealThe Kickr Climb lets you simulate gradients of up to 20%, by literally lifting the front of your bike up and down, to make things feel all the more realistic. It's a useful addition to your setup if you're trying to train for riding up long climbs and you want to mimic the position. View DealThe Roam barely needs an introduction. It's the goldilocks GPS in Wahoo's range, balancing price, screen size and battery life nicely. View DealThis one's the baby of the range. More of a racer's choice, but it also packs more or less all the features of the Roam into a smaller, cheaper package.View DealAnd finally, if you want the biggest screen possible for your bike computer then it has to be the Elemnt Ace. It's really very large, the battery is bigger, but of course, so is the price. View DealYou can easily make do with a simple fan for indoor training, but if you want to have a better time you can get a smart fan like the Kickr Headwind. It'll either work as a dumb fan (just turn it up and down as needed) or you can set it to increase power in line with with your heart rate monitor, so it'll blow stronger the harder you ride. View DealOur other Black Friday 2026 roundups👕 : With 25% off sitewide, we've rounded up our favourite items from the British brand.💾 : A live, ever-changing roundup of our favourite deals on Garmin's bike computers, smartwatches, heart rate monitors and more, from Garmin's own site and beyond.

Wall Street Reels as AI Fears Erupt; Nasdaq 100 Near Bear Market
item.author: Judy Lagrou and Geoffrey Morgan
item.content:encoded: Wall Street reeled on Friday as nagging concerns about the AI trade, which propelled US stocks from one high to the next for much of the year, turned into a full-blown, market-wide selloff. Anthropic PBC slumped after soaring in its public-market debut, while Nvidia Corp. sank 14%, pushing the Nasdaq 100 to the brink of a bear market.

item.title: An entrepreneur fights for workers’ protections after his mom was fired after being assaulted at her Saks Fifth Avenue job
item.author: Victoria Bekiempis in New York
item.content:encoded: Jeff Vinokur is using his newly minted wealth from the sale of his edtech company to hold the retail store accountableLate in the afternoon of 28 June, Jeff Vinokur received a call from his mother that sent him running. “I was assaulted,” Vinokur, a popular science educator known as the “Dancing Scientist”, recalled his mother saying.Vinokur’s mother, Laza Susuni, was working in the women’s ready-to-wear section at Manhattan’s Saks Fifth Avenue that day when a client attacked her in the dressing room. A court document reviewed by the Guardian corroborates that a woman was arrested at that location on assault and harassment charges.Continue reading...
